glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.lead: Every technical term from the six topics, in alphabetical order. Data-science terms have a longer explanation for readers who know Java but not machine learning.
glossary.filter.label: Filter terms
glossary.filter.placeholder: Type a term, for example batch
glossary.internal.hint: A name we coined for this project, not a standard term. Papers and textbooks may call the same idea something else.
term.activation-function.name: Activation function
term.activation-function.short: A simple non-linear function after a layer; without it a stack of layers collapses into one matrix multiplication.
term.activation-function.long: Matrix multiplications chained together are still one matrix multiplication, so a network of them could learn only straight-line relationships. An activation function bends the result after each layer. This network uses two: ReLU inside the trunk and tanh at the end of the value head. Both are cheap per element, so they cost almost nothing next to the matrix work.
term.adam.name: Adam
term.adam.short: An optimiser that scales each weight's step by running averages of its recent gradients and their squares.
term.adam.long: Adam (Kingma and Ba) keeps two running averages per weight: of the gradient, like momentum, and of the squared gradient. Dividing one by the square root of the other gives every weight a step of similar size, whatever the scale of its gradients. That makes it work over a wide range of learning rates. AdamW, the project's default, builds on it.
term.adamw.name: AdamW
term.adamw.short: Adam with weight decay applied separately from the gradient; the project's default optimiser.
term.adamw.long: AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter) fixes how Adam handles weight decay: it shrinks the weights directly instead of mixing the decay into the scaled gradient. The project uses beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999, epsilon {sci:1e-8} and weight decay 0.01 on weight tensors only. Adam-style scaling suits this network because it has no normalisation layers, so gradient scales differ by orders of magnitude.
term.adjudication.name: Adjudication
term.adjudication.short: Ending a game early with a result that is already proven or clear, instead of playing it out.
term.alpha-beta.name: Alpha-beta pruning
term.alpha-beta.short: Minimax with two bounds, alpha and beta, that skips moves which cannot change the result: same move, far fewer nodes.
term.aspiration-window.name: Aspiration window
term.aspiration-window.short: Start a search iteration with a narrow window, here ±50, around the previous score; widen it fourfold on a miss.
term.backend.name: Backend
term.backend.short: The code that runs the forward pass behind `NetBackend`: Java scalar, Vector API, TornadoVM, C++ WebAssembly or WebGPU.
term.backpropagation.name: Backpropagation
term.backpropagation.short: Computes all gradients in one pass backwards through the layers, using the chain rule.
term.backpropagation.long: After a forward pass, backpropagation walks the layers in reverse order. Each layer receives the gradient of the loss with respect to its output and returns the gradient with respect to its input and its weights. Forward and backward pass together cost about three times the work of a forward pass alone.
term.batch.name: Batch
term.batch.short: Several samples or positions processed together in one step or one network call; 256 in training, 1 in CPU MCTS.
term.batch.long: A batch is the unit of work of a network call. In training, the gradient is averaged over a batch of 256 samples per step. In inference, a GPU is fast only with large batches: TornadoVM reached about {n:2000} evaluations per second one at a time and about {n:111000} at batch 256. A CPU gains nothing, and MCTS loses strength when it batches leaves.
term.bayesian-optimisation.name: Bayesian optimisation
term.bayesian-optimisation.short: A tuner that models result versus settings and picks the next trial from that model; not used here.
term.bayesian-optimisation.long: Bayesian optimisation fits a statistical model, often a Gaussian process, to the trials so far. The model predicts the result of untried settings and how uncertain that prediction is. The next trial goes where a good result is likely or the uncertainty is high. It saves trials when each one is expensive. This project did not use it.
term.beam-search.name: Beam search
term.beam-search.short: Keeps only the k best partial plans per step (here 200 or 300); plays race positions outside the table.
term.branching-factor.name: Branching factor
term.branching-factor.short: The number of legal moves in a position: 14 at the start, 54 in this site's mid-game position.
term.canonical-orientation.name: Canonical orientation
term.canonical-orientation.short: The encoder rotates the board so the player to move always starts at the top; one network serves every seat.
term.capacity.name: Capacity
term.capacity.short: How much a network can represent, roughly its number of weights: SMALL about {n:62000}, LARGE about {n:353000}.
term.capacity.long: A network with too little capacity cannot fit even its training data; one with too much can memorise it. The capacity test trained four sizes from scratch on the same data and set its go/no-go rule in advance. The LARGE network (64 channels, 6 blocks) beat the best network of loop run 3 by +138 Elo and moved into the loop.
term.channel.name: Channel
term.channel.short: One number per cell in a tensor, like a column of a table row; the SMALL trunk has 32.
term.channel.long: If a tensor is a table with one row per cell, a channel is one of its columns. Input channels have a fixed meaning that the encoder computes, such as 'my piece here'. Inside the trunk, the network decides during training what each of its 32 channels means (64 in LARGE); nobody assigns them a meaning by hand.
term.checkpoint.name: Checkpoint
term.checkpoint.short: A saved snapshot of weights and optimiser state, written atomically, so a killed training run resumes bit for bit.
term.clopper-pearson.name: Clopper-Pearson bound
term.clopper-pearson.short: An exact bound on a rate from a count; 1 error in 993 adjudications bounds the rate at 0.477 %.
term.clopper-pearson.long: A rate measured from few events is uncertain, and the usual normal approximation fails when failures are rare. The Clopper-Pearson interval comes from the binomial distribution directly, so it stays valid there. The project used its one-sided upper bound to accept the adjudication margin: one wrong verdict in 993 firings bounds the error rate at 0.477 %.
term.confidence-interval.name: Confidence interval
term.confidence-interval.short: A range built to contain the true value in 95 % of repeated experiments; written as ± after Elo.
term.confidence-interval.long: A match measures strength with noise, so a single number would claim too much. The interval states the uncertainty: +66.8 ± 16.0 Elo means 50.8 to 82.8. If the interval excludes 0, chance alone is an unlikely explanation of the difference. Intervals near a score of 1 get wide, because their upper end hits the score clamp at 0.999.
term.convolution.name: Convolution
term.convolution.short: The same small weight matrix applied at every cell to the cell and its neighbours, finding local patterns anywhere.
term.convolution.long: A convolution slides one shared weight matrix over the whole board. At each cell it combines that cell with its neighbours, so a pattern such as 'a piece that can jump' is found wherever it occurs, with weights learned once. Image networks use it on square pixel grids; this project needed its own version, the hex convolution, for the star board.
term.cosine-decay.name: Cosine decay
term.cosine-decay.short: Lowers the learning rate along half a cosine curve, from its base value to a small final value.
term.cosine-decay.long: A cosine decay keeps the learning rate high for a while, then lowers it ever faster through the middle and flattens out near the final value. Large early steps make progress, small late steps settle the weights. The schedule comes from Loshchilov and Hutter (SGDR). Sweep 1 found that cosine {sci:3e-4} to {sci:1e-5} over {n:15000} steps ended the stall of loop run 2.
term.cross-entropy.name: Cross-entropy
term.cross-entropy.short: The standard loss for comparing two probability distributions; used for the policy.
term.cross-entropy.long: Cross-entropy is −Σ target(m) · log(predicted(m)) over the moves m. It is small when the network gives high probability to the moves the target prefers and grows fast when it gives a preferred move almost none. Its minimum depends on the target, so the project reports the KL divergence, the cross-entropy minus that minimum.
term.cut-off.name: Cut-off
term.cut-off.short: The moment `alpha >= beta` in alpha-beta: the remaining moves of that node are skipped.
term.data-augmentation.name: Data augmentation
term.data-augmentation.short: Extra samples from a transformation that keeps the meaning; here the left-right mirror of two-player positions.
term.data-augmentation.long: If a transformation does not change what a position means, it yields a new sample for free. The star board is symmetric left to right, so training mirrors two-player samples at random, together with their move targets. The network sees more variety without a single extra game. Rotations are not needed, because the encoder already fixes the orientation.
term.devenv-task.name: devenv task
term.devenv-task.short: A named step in `devenv.nix` that runs one script after the tasks it depends on.
term.dirichlet-noise.name: Dirichlet noise
term.dirichlet-noise.short: Random noise on the root priors in self-play, so the search also tries moves the network dislikes; off in play.
term.dirichlet-noise.long: At the root of each self-play search, the priors are mixed with random numbers from a Dirichlet distribution, here with alpha 0.3 and weight 0.25, following common AlphaZero practice. Without it, self-play would keep replaying the moves the network already likes and never learn whether others are better. In games against you the noise is off.
term.elo.name: Elo
term.elo.short: A rating scale: D points of difference mean an expected score of 1 / (1 + 10^(−D/400)).
term.elo.long: Elo turns a match score into a strength difference, `400 · log10(s / (1 − s))`. A score of 0.5 is 0 Elo, about 0.64 is +100. The project gives every Elo number with a 95 % interval and clamps the score to 0.001 … 0.999, so the largest possible value is ±1200. Near a score of 1 the curve is steep, so large Elo numbers are imprecise.
term.emscripten.name: Emscripten
term.emscripten.short: The toolchain that compiles C and C++ to WebAssembly; it builds the C++ engine and the browser's forward pass.
term.engine.name: Engine
term.engine.short: A program that picks a move for a given position; here either classical alpha-beta or a network with MCTS.
term.epoch.name: Epoch
term.epoch.short: One pass over all training samples; 4 epochs means each sample was seen about four times.
term.epoch.long: Epochs measure how often training revisited its data. Run 1 of generation 0 trained 4 epochs on {n:4300} games and stayed weak; run 2 used about five times the data in about 2.2 epochs and played better. More passes over the same data cannot replace new data. In the loop, the reuse factor plays the role of epochs.
term.equal-cost.name: Equal cost
term.equal-cost.short: A slower candidate gets nodes scaled by its measured speed ratio, so both sides spend the same CPU time.
term.evaluation-function.name: Evaluation function
term.evaluation-function.short: A function that scores a position without searching further; the search calls it at the leaves.
term.exploration-exploitation.name: Exploration vs exploitation
term.exploration-exploitation.short: Trying less-known options to learn about them, versus choosing the option that currently looks best.
term.exploration-exploitation.long: Every search and every learner faces this trade-off. Pure exploitation never discovers a better move; pure exploration wastes effort on bad ones. In PUCT the constant `c` sets the balance between the average result and the prior bonus. In self-play, Dirichlet noise and temperature push towards exploration, so training sees moves the network would not pick on its own.
term.f32-f16.name: F32 and F16
term.f32-f16.short: 32-bit and 16-bit floating-point numbers; the models are stored as F16 and computed in F32.
term.f32-f16.long: F32 is Java's `float`; F16 has half the bits, so less precision and range. The project packs the weights as F16 and compresses them with gzip, which shrinks the expert model from about {n:250} kB to {n:115} kB. The browser widens them back to F32 before it computes. On {n:2000} test positions the F16 model picked the same best move every time.
term.feature.name: Feature
term.feature.short: One number that describes a position, such as the summed distance, used as an input of a learned formula.
term.feature.long: A feature is a hand-made measurement of a position, always counted as side to move minus opponent: the summed distance to the goal, the last straggler, pieces at home, useful jumps. The linear evaluation multiplies each of its 13 features by a weight and adds them up. Choosing features is human work; finding their weights is the data-science part.
term.flop.name: FLOP
term.flop.short: One floating-point operation, such as a multiplication or addition; a SMALL forward pass needs about 14 million per position.
term.flop.long: FLOPs count the arithmetic work of a computation independent of the hardware. Dividing a model's FLOPs per position by a device's measured evaluations per second shows how well a backend uses the device. For the SMALL network about 14 million FLOPs per position means that {n:1000} evaluations per second need about 14 billion operations per second.
term.forward-pass.name: Forward pass
term.forward-pass.short: One evaluation of the network: input planes in, policy and value out.
term.forward-pass.long: A forward pass sends a batch of encoded positions through all layers in order and returns, per position, the priors of the legal moves and a value per player. For the SMALL network it costs about 14 million floating-point operations per position. In the browser it runs in C++ WebAssembly or on WebGPU; the search around it stays in Java.
term.futility-pruning.name: Futility pruning
term.futility-pruning.short: Near the leaves, skip moves whose optimistic bound, the static score plus a margin, still cannot reach alpha.
term.game-tree.name: Game tree
term.game-tree.short: Positions as nodes and moves as edges, grown from the current position as the root.
term.gate.name: Gate
term.gate.short: A match of candidate against best network; the candidate is promoted only if `score − 1.28 · se > 0.5`.
term.generation.name: Generation
term.generation.short: One cycle of self-play, training and gate; generation 0 learned from the classical engine.
term.gradient.name: Gradient
term.gradient.short: For every weight, the direction and size of the change of the loss when that weight grows.
term.gradient.long: The gradient is a vector with one entry per weight: the partial derivative of the loss with respect to that weight. A positive entry means 'the loss rises if this weight grows'. Backpropagation computes all entries at once, and gradient descent steps against them. For the SMALL network the gradient has as many entries as the parameters, about {n:62000}.
term.gradient-descent.name: Gradient descent
term.gradient-descent.short: Repeatedly moves every weight a small step against its gradient, so that the loss falls.
term.gradient-descent.long: Gradient descent is a hill climber that walks downhill: compute the gradient on a batch, move each weight a little in the opposite direction, repeat. The learning rate sets the step size. Because each batch is a random sample, the steps are noisy, which is why the variant used in practice is called stochastic gradient descent (SGD).
term.grid-search.name: Grid search
term.grid-search.short: Trying every combination of a few chosen values for a few settings.
term.grid-search.long: Grid search is the simplest tuner: pick a few values per setting and test all combinations. It is easy to read and repeat, but the cost grows with the product of the value counts. This project ran only small grids, chosen by a person and judged in the arena, such as 14 settings of the three futility margins.
term.held-out-set.name: Held-out set
term.held-out-set.short: Data kept out of training and used only to measure, like a test set the code under test never saw.
term.held-out-set.long: A model can fit its training data and still fail on new data. A held-out set detects that: it never takes part in fitting and only measures afterwards. The classical evaluation was checked on 400 held-out games, and the network training keeps every 10th game out. Good numbers on held-out data are necessary, but in this project only matches decide.
term.heuristic.name: Heuristic
term.heuristic.short: A fast estimate that is usually right but not exact, such as the pieces' summed distance to the goal.
term.hex-convolution.name: Hex convolution
term.hex-convolution.short: The project's convolution for the star board: gather each cell and its 6 neighbours, then multiply by one matrix.
term.hex-convolution.long: The hex convolution has two steps. Gather: for each of the 121 cells, copy the channels of the cell and of its 6 neighbours into one vector, using a precomputed `int[121][7]` table. Off-board neighbours point at a padding row of zeros, so there are no special cases. Then multiply each vector by one weight matrix and add a bias.
term.hilla.name: Hilla
term.hilla.short: Vaadin's framework for React front ends with typed calls to Spring endpoints; it carries the online mode.
term.history-heuristic.name: History heuristic
term.history-heuristic.short: An ordering hint that prefers moves which caused cut-offs often during the whole search, not only at the same height.
term.hyperparameter.name: Hyperparameter
term.hyperparameter.short: A setting that training or search does not learn by itself, such as the learning rate or the node budget.
term.hyperparameter.long: A model learns its weights from data; a hyperparameter is chosen from outside: the learning rate, the batch size, the PUCT constant `c`, the node budget. In Java terms, the weights are the state an object builds up while it runs, and the hyperparameters are its constructor arguments. Topic 5 shows how this project set each one, from a plain choice to a rule fixed in advance.
term.inference.name: Inference
term.inference.short: Running a network forward with fixed weights to get its outputs, as a game does; training changes the weights instead.
term.inference.long: Inference and training are the two modes of a network. Inference evaluates it: positions in, priors and values out, weights untouched. Every game in the app only does inference. Training runs the network forward too, then computes gradients backwards and updates the weights; that costs about three times the work of a forward pass per example.
term.input-plane.name: Input plane
term.input-plane.short: One input channel computed from the position, for example 1 where the player to move has a piece.
term.input-plane.long: The encoder turns a position into input planes, one value per cell each. Seven plain planes hold the pieces of each player, the goal and start corner, the playable cells and the game's progress. The plane set `classic1` adds six planes with classical knowledge such as distances and the linear evaluation, 13 in all. The shared model for four variants reads 15.
term.iterative-deepening.name: Iterative deepening
term.iterative-deepening.short: Search depth 1, then 2, then 3, keeping the last finished answer, so the search can stop at any budget.
term.killer-move.name: Killer move
term.killer-move.short: A move that caused a cut-off at the same height (plies below the root) before; the search tries it early.
term.kl-divergence.name: KL divergence
term.kl-divergence.short: A measure of how different two probability distributions are; 0 exactly when they are equal.
term.kl-divergence.long: The Kullback-Leibler divergence is the cross-entropy of two distributions minus the entropy of the target. Unlike cross-entropy, its minimum is 0 for every position, so numbers from different positions compare well. The project reports it for the policy: how far the network's move distribution is from the target. It also showed that F16 weights barely change the priors.
term.ladder.name: Ladder (rung)
term.ladder.short: Fixed classical opponents: each rung is `BEST_SPEC` limited to N nodes per move, such as {n:25600} or {n:102400}.
term.late-move-reductions.name: Late move reductions (LMR)
term.late-move-reductions.short: Search late, probably weak moves less deep first, and re-search them at full depth only if they look good.
term.layer.name: Layer
term.layer.short: One step of the network that turns a tensor into a new one, such as a hex convolution.
term.layer.long: A network is a pipeline of layers, much like a chain of stream operations. Each layer takes a tensor and returns a new one. Here there are only a few kinds: hex convolution, dense layer (a plain matrix multiplication), mean over cells, and the activation functions. Keeping the kinds few lets every backend, from Java to WGSL, implement them all.
term.leaf-batching.name: Leaf batching
term.leaf-batching.short: Collecting several new leaves before one forward pass; it costs strength, so the browser CPU uses batch 1.
term.learning-rate.name: Learning rate
term.learning-rate.short: The step size of gradient descent; a constant {sci:3e-4} stalled loop run 2, a cosine decay fixed it.
term.learning-rate.long: Too large a learning rate makes the loss jump around or explode; too small makes training crawl. It is rarely constant: a warm-up raises it, a decay lowers it. In this project the constant {sci:3e-4} of loop run 2 stalled the loop, while a cosine from {sci:3e-4} to {sci:1e-5} over {n:15000} steps on the same data beat the start network.
term.log-loss.name: Log loss
term.log-loss.short: The cross-entropy of a probability forecast: small when the predicted win probabilities match the actual results.
term.log-loss.long: Log loss scores a forecast by −log of the probability it gave to what actually happened. A confident wrong forecast costs a lot, a cautious one little. It is the quantity that logistic regression minimises. In this project a refit with the lower held-out log loss still played weaker, so the tournament, not the loss, decided which weights stayed.
term.logistic-regression.name: Logistic regression
term.logistic-regression.short: Fits weights so that the sigmoid of a weighted feature sum predicts a win probability.
term.logistic-regression.long: Logistic regression is the standard model for yes/no outcomes. It computes a weighted sum of features and passes it through the sigmoid to get a probability. Fitting chooses the weights that make the observed outcomes most likely. Here the outcome is a win, the rows are about {n:68000} positions from {n:2000} games, and the fitted weights became the linear evaluation.
term.logit.name: Logit
term.logit.short: A raw score before it becomes a probability; strictly, the log of the odds p / (1 − p).
term.logit.long: Any real number can be a logit; higher means more likely. Strictly it is log(p / (1 − p)), and the sigmoid turns it back into p. The linear evaluation is a logit of the win probability. The network's policy head outputs one logit per legal move, and a softmax turns these logits into probabilities that sum to 1.
term.loss.name: Loss
term.loss.short: One number that measures how wrong the network is on a batch; training makes it smaller.
term.loss.long: The loss function turns the difference between outputs and targets into a single number, like a test that does not pass or fail but returns a score to push down. Here it is the sum of a policy loss, the cross-entropy, and a value loss, the mean squared error. Gradient descent changes the weights in the direction that lowers it.
term.mate-score.name: Mate score
term.mate-score.short: A score for a win h plies below the root: `MATE - h`, so shorter wins score higher.
term.mcts.name: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)
term.mcts.short: A search that grows the game tree one simulation at a time and spends more simulations on promising moves.
term.minimax.name: Minimax
term.minimax.short: Choose the move that is best for you, assuming the opponent always answers with their own best move.
term.move-ordering.name: Move ordering
term.move-ordering.short: Searching the likely best moves first, so alpha-beta cuts off earlier; here the table move, killer moves, then distance gain.
term.mse.name: Mean squared error (MSE)
term.mse.short: The average of (prediction − target)²; used for the value.
term.mse.long: Mean squared error is the usual loss for a number to predict. Squaring makes large misses cost much more than small ones and makes the loss smooth, which suits gradient descent. Here the value head predicts a result in −1 to +1 per player, and the MSE compares it with the value target.
term.negamax.name: Negamax
term.negamax.short: Minimax as one recursive function: scores count from the side to move, so `score = -negamax(child)`.
term.neural-network.name: Neural network
term.neural-network.short: A pure function with many learned numbers that maps a board to move priors and a value per player.
term.neural-network.long: For a Java developer, a neural network is a function whose code never changes; its behaviour sits in about {n:62000} numbers, the parameters. It is built from layers, each a matrix multiplication plus a simple non-linear step. Training adjusts the numbers until the outputs fit many examples. Here the input is the encoded board, the outputs are a policy and a value.
term.node.name: Node
term.node.short: One position visited by a search; in the classical engine one call of `negamax`, the unit of the node budget.
term.node-budget.name: Node budget
term.node-budget.short: The number of nodes a player may visit per move; the app's five strength levels are node budgets.
term.node-limit.name: Node limit
term.node-limit.short: Strength runs fix the nodes or simulations per move instead of a time, so machine load cannot change results.
term.optimiser.name: Optimiser
term.optimiser.short: The algorithm that turns gradients into weight updates, for example SGD with momentum or AdamW.
term.optimiser.long: Plain gradient descent subtracts learning rate times gradient. An optimiser refines that rule: momentum averages recent gradients, Adam also scales each weight's step by the size of its recent gradients, AdamW adds weight decay separately. The project's trainer offers AdamW as default and SGD with momentum as the second choice. Each new candidate starts with a fresh optimiser.
term.overfitting.name: Overfitting
term.overfitting.short: A model fits its training data better and new data worse, because it has learned noise instead of patterns.
term.overfitting.long: Overfitting shows as a gap: the loss on training data falls while the held-out loss stays or rises. In loop run 5 the training value loss was 0.21 against 0.457 held out. For the classical evaluation the risk was weights that fit self-play only, so later refits also had to beat a different evaluator family.
term.paired-games.name: Paired games
term.paired-games.short: Two games from the same random opening with the sides swapped, so the luck of the opening cancels out.
term.parameters.name: Parameters
term.parameters.short: All learned numbers of a network, its weights and biases; the expert model has about {n:62000}.
term.parameters.long: The parameters are the whole learned state of a network. Counting them gives its size: the SMALL network with the plane set `classic1` has {n:61734}, the LARGE one {n:352998}. As 32-bit floats the expert model takes about 250 kB, as F16 half that. The rest of the network is fixed code, so loading a model means loading its parameters.
term.paranoid-search.name: Paranoid search
term.paranoid-search.short: Three-player search that treats both opponents as one coalition, so alpha-beta applies again.
term.passed-position.name: Passed position
term.passed-position.short: Both armies have passed each other, so no piece can block or jump over a foreign piece any more.
term.plateau.name: Plateau
term.plateau.short: The point where a learning curve stops rising, as loop run 3 did after about 8 to 9 generations.
term.plateau.long: A plateau means the current recipe has run out of gains: more of the same no longer helps. Loop run 3 climbed to +354 ± 54 Elo against {n:102400} nodes at generation 9 and then stopped rising. The project read this as the limit of the SMALL network and the recipe, and tested a larger network next.
term.ply.name: Ply
term.ply.short: One move by one side; depth 4 means 4 plies, two for each side.
term.policy.name: Policy
term.policy.short: The network's probability for each legal move: which moves look good in this position.
term.policy.long: The policy is one of the network's two outputs, a probability distribution over the legal moves. You can read it as 'which move would a strong player pick?'. MCTS uses it as the prior that decides which moves to look at first. In training, the policy target comes from the teacher's scores or from the visit counts of a self-play search.
term.post-message.name: postMessage
term.post-message.short: The browser call that sends a message between page and worker; the data are copied or transferred, never shared.
term.pre-registration.name: Pre-registration
term.pre-registration.short: A decision rule fixed before the experiment runs, so the result cannot quietly move the goal.
term.pre-registration.long: When the rule comes after the data, it is easy to pick a threshold that makes the result look good. Pre-registration writes it down first. This project did so for the capacity test (KL at least 0.03 lower and gate at least 0.58), for the simulation count (+80 Elo per doubling) and for the stop rule that ended training after loop run 7.
term.principal-variation-search.name: Principal variation search (PVS)
term.principal-variation-search.short: Search the first move with a full window, the rest with a minimal one that only proves 'not better'.
term.prior.name: Prior
term.prior.short: A probability given to a move before the search looks at it; the search corrects it with visit counts.
term.prior.long: A prior is a guess made in advance. In MCTS the network's policy gives every legal move a prior P, and the PUCT rule uses it to decide which moves to try first. As visits add up, the measured average result Q takes over. The residual priors are a different idea: two learned numbers that add classical knowledge to the network's outputs.
term.proxy-metric.name: Proxy metric
term.proxy-metric.short: A cheap quality number on held-out positions, such as top-1 agreement or winner prediction, instead of a match.
term.proxy-metric.long: Matches are the real test of a network but cost hours. Proxy metrics cost seconds: how often the network's favourite move equals the target's (top-1), how often the value predicts the actual winner, and the KL divergence. In sweep 1 they hardly told the eight recipes apart, while the gate did, so the gate stayed the criterion.
term.puct.name: PUCT
term.puct.short: The MCTS selection rule: average result Q plus a bonus for moves with a high prior and few visits.
term.puct.long: PUCT scores each move as `Q + c · P · sqrt(N_parent) / (1 + N)`. Q is the move's average result, P its prior, N its visits, N_parent those of the position above. The first term rewards moves that worked, the second moves the network likes but the search rarely tried. The constant `c` sets the balance; 1.0 measured best, within the noise of 0.5 to 1.5.
term.pwa.name: PWA (progressive web app)
term.pwa.short: A website that you can install and use offline, thanks to a service worker and a web manifest.
term.quantization.name: Quantization
term.quantization.short: Storing weights with fewer bits to save space; here only F16 storage, no integer quantization.
term.quantization.long: Quantization trades precision for size and speed: weights stored as 16-bit or 8-bit numbers instead of 32-bit floats. Integer schemes need scale factors and sometimes retraining. This project uses only the mildest form, F16 storage widened back to F32 for computing, and measured that the priors barely change: a mean KL divergence of {sci:3e-7} to {sci:5e-7}.
term.race-table.name: Race table
term.race-table.short: The project's tablebase: the exact number of moves to fill the goal for each placement of 10 pieces near it.
term.random-search.name: Random search
term.random-search.short: Trying randomly drawn combinations of settings instead of a fixed grid; not used in this project.
term.random-search.long: Random search draws each trial's settings at random from given ranges. When only a few of many settings matter, it tests more distinct values of those few than a grid of the same size. It needs no model and parallelises trivially. This project did not use it; all its searches were small grids.
term.ranking-function.name: Ranking function
term.ranking-function.short: A one-to-one map from a piece placement to an array index, so the table stores values only and no keys.
term.relu.name: ReLU
term.relu.short: The activation `max(0, x)`: negative values become 0, positive ones pass unchanged.
term.relu.long: ReLU (rectified linear unit) is the most common activation function. It keeps positive values and sets negative ones to 0, which is enough non-linearity for deep stacks to learn. This network applies it after every convolution of the trunk and once inside the value head. In code it is one comparison per element.
term.replay-buffer.name: Replay buffer
term.replay-buffer.short: An in-memory window of recent samples that evicts the oldest whole generation, like a bounded queue.
term.replay-buffer.long: Training on only the newest games would make the network forget what older games taught it. The replay buffer keeps a window of recent samples, here {n:500000} by default and 2 million in loop run 4, and training draws random batches from all of it. When the window is full, the oldest generation leaves as a whole.
term.residual-block.name: Residual block
term.residual-block.short: Two convolutions whose output is added to the block's input, so the block only learns a correction.
term.residual-block.long: A residual block computes `ReLU(conv2(ReLU(conv1(x))) + x)`. Because the input x is added back through a skip connection, the block starts out as almost the identity and only has to learn what to change. This idea from ResNet (He et al., 2015) keeps deeper stacks trainable. The SMALL network has 4 such blocks, the LARGE one 6.
term.retrograde-analysis.name: Retrograde analysis
term.retrograde-analysis.short: Builds a table backwards from the final positions, one move layer at a time, like breadth-first search on reversed moves.
term.reuse-factor.name: Reuse factor
term.reuse-factor.short: How many times, on average, each new sample is drawn per generation: `steps = ceil(R · new samples / batch)`.
term.reuse-factor.long: The reuse factor R ties the training effort to the amount of fresh data. With R = 4 and batch 256, every 64 new samples add one training step. Higher R squeezes more out of each game but risks overfitting to it. The default is 4, loop run 4 used 20, and the best value was never measured.
term.safetensors.name: safetensors
term.safetensors.short: A file format for tensors: 8 bytes header length, a JSON header with names and shapes, then the raw bytes.
term.saturation.name: Saturation
term.saturation.short: An opponent that is beaten almost every time, above a score of about 0.85, no longer shows differences.
term.saturation.long: Near a score of 1 the Elo curve is steep and the standard error is large in Elo, so a match against a much weaker opponent cannot resolve a gain. Loop run 4 scored 0.82 to 0.91 against the classical ladder and showed no gain there, while a direct match against its start network found +78 ± 19 Elo. Saturation then calls for a stronger opponent.
term.seed.name: Seed
term.seed.short: The start value of a random generator; the same seed gives the same openings and batches, so runs repeat.
term.selection-bias.name: Selection bias
term.selection-bias.short: Picking the best of many noisy results overestimates it; the winner has to be confirmed on fresh data.
term.selection-bias.long: If eight recipes are equally good, one of them still scores highest by luck, and its score is too high. The more candidates, the larger the effect. The cure is a second measurement that the selection did not see. Sweep 1 confirmed its winner, variant F, on 400 fresh pairs at 0.5887 (standard error 0.0136), about +62 Elo.
term.self-play.name: Self-play
term.self-play.short: The program plays against itself to produce its own training data; here the best network plays both sides with MCTS.
term.self-play.long: Self-play is like a load test that generates its own traffic: no human games are needed. The best network plays both sides with MCTS, and every position becomes a training sample whose policy target is the search's visit distribution and whose value target is the game result. A better network gives better searches, which give better targets for the next one.
term.service-worker.name: Service worker
term.service-worker.short: A browser script between page and network that caches the site's files, so the site also works offline.
term.sgd-momentum.name: SGD with momentum
term.sgd-momentum.short: Stochastic gradient descent that steps along a running average of recent gradients, like inertia.
term.sgd-momentum.long: Momentum keeps a velocity per weight: each step adds the new gradient to a decaying sum of the old ones and moves along that sum. Noise from single batches cancels out, and steady directions speed up. The trainer offers it with momentum 0.9 as the second optimiser; AdamW is the default because gradient scales differ strongly between the layers of this network.
term.sigmoid.name: Sigmoid
term.sigmoid.short: The function 1 / (1 + e^−x); it turns any number into a probability between 0 and 1.
term.sigmoid.long: The sigmoid is an S-shaped curve: very negative inputs give almost 0, 0 gives 0.5, very positive inputs give almost 1. Logistic regression uses it to read a weighted sum as a probability. The linear evaluation of this project is such a sum, scaled by 100: a score of +179 means sigmoid(1.79), a win probability of about 0.86.
term.simd.name: SIMD
term.simd.short: One CPU instruction works on several numbers at once, for example 4 floats in 128-bit WebAssembly SIMD.
term.simulation.name: Simulation
term.simulation.short: One MCTS walk from the root to a new position, one network evaluation and one backup of the result.
term.softmax.name: Softmax
term.softmax.short: Turns a list of logits into probabilities that sum to 1; here only over the legal moves.
term.softmax.long: Softmax computes `exp(l_i) / Σ exp(l_j)`: every logit becomes positive, larger logits get a larger share, and the shares sum to 1. The policy head applies it only over the legal moves, so illegal moves never get a probability. Generation 0 uses it a second way: it turns the teacher's move scores into the policy target.
term.spec-string.name: Spec string
term.spec-string.short: A text that configures a player, such as `ab:eval=racelin1-r3,pvs=1,…`; each key switches a search option.
term.sprt.name: SPRT
term.sprt.short: Sequential probability ratio test: stops a match as soon as the games decide between two Elo hypotheses.
term.sprt.long: A fixed-size match wastes games when the result is clear early. SPRT checks after each game how much more likely the results are under one Elo hypothesis, elo1, than under the other, elo0, and stops when the ratio crosses a bound. The arena offers it with alpha = beta = 0.05 for quick tuning loops; verifier runs play a fixed number of pairs.
term.spsa.name: SPSA
term.spsa.short: Simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation: nudges all settings at once by random signs and follows the measured gain; not used here.
term.spsa.long: SPSA estimates a gradient from just two measurements per step: play with all settings shifted by +δ in random directions, then by −δ, and compare. It then moves every setting a little towards the better side. Chess engines use it to tune many search parameters through games. This project did not use it.
term.standard-error.name: Standard error
term.standard-error.short: How much a mean score could vary by chance; it shrinks with the square root of the number of pairs.
term.standard-error.long: Play the same match again with new openings and the mean score comes out a little different. The standard error estimates that spread: the standard deviation of the pair scores divided by the square root of the number of pairs. The gate subtracts 1.28 standard errors before it compares the score with 0.5, and the 95 % intervals come from about ±1.96 standard errors of the score.
term.supervised-learning.name: Supervised learning
term.supervised-learning.short: Learning from examples whose answers come from a known source; here the classical engine `BEST_SPEC`.
term.supervised-learning.long: In supervised learning every example comes with the answer the model should give, like a unit test with an expected value. Generation 0 learned this way: `BEST_SPEC` played the games, a second search scored every legal move, and the network learned to predict these scores and the results. Self-play replaces the teacher with the network's own search later.
term.tablebase.name: Tablebase
term.tablebase.short: A precomputed table with the exact value of every position of a class; here the race table.
term.tanh.name: tanh
term.tanh.short: The hyperbolic tangent: it squashes any number into the range −1 to +1, the range of game results.
term.tanh.long: tanh is an S-shaped curve like the sigmoid, but centred on 0 with outputs between −1 and +1. The value head ends with it because a game result lies in that range: −1 a certain loss, +1 a certain win. With the residual priors, the classical evaluation is added before the tanh, so the network starts from the classical judgement.
term.target.name: Target (label)
term.target.short: The expected answer stored with a training sample, like the expected value in a unit test.
term.target.long: The network's output is compared with the target, and the loss measures the difference. Each sample here has two targets: a policy target with a probability per legal move, and a value target with a result per player. In generation 0 they come from the classical teacher; in self-play from the visit counts and the final result.
term.teavm.name: TeaVM
term.teavm.short: An ahead-of-time compiler from JVM bytecode to JavaScript and WebAssembly; it brings the Java search into the browser.
term.temperature.name: Temperature
term.temperature.short: How random a choice from a distribution is; early in self-play, moves are drawn in proportion to visit counts.
term.temperature.long: At temperature 1, a move with twice the visits is drawn twice as often; near 0, the most visited move always wins. Self-play uses temperature 1 for the first 14 plies, so games differ, and then plays the most visited move. The prior temperature of MCTS and the teacher temperature of generation 0 apply the same idea to other distributions.
term.tensor.name: Tensor
term.tensor.short: A multi-dimensional array with a shape; in this project a flat `float[]` plus a shape such as `[122][13]`.
term.tensor.long: A tensor is the data type that flows between layers. Its shape lists the size of each dimension: the board is `[122][13]`, 122 rows of 13 numbers. The project stores every tensor as one flat `float[]` and computes the index of element (row, channel) as `row · C + channel`, the same way you would flatten a matrix by hand.
term.texel-tuning.name: Texel tuning
term.texel-tuning.short: The chess-programming name for fitting evaluation weights to game results by logistic regression.
term.tornadovm.name: TornadoVM
term.tornadovm.short: A JVM plug-in that compiles Java methods into GPU kernels at run time; used for training and server play.
term.training-sample.name: Training sample
term.training-sample.short: One labelled row: a position, its policy target and value target, plus two weights that can switch a target off.
term.training-sample.long: A training sample is to the network what a row of labelled data is to a regression. The input is the position from the mover's view; the answers are a probability per legal move and a result per player. On disk a sample takes about 479 bytes; the input planes are rebuilt from the cells when a batch is assembled.
term.training-step.name: Step (training step)
term.training-step.short: One update of all weights from the gradient of one batch.
term.training-step.long: Training counts its work in steps. Each step draws one batch, computes the loss and its gradients, and lets the optimiser update every weight once. The learning-rate schedule is a function of the step number. In the loop, the number of steps per generation follows from the reuse factor: `steps = ceil(R · new samples / batch)`.
term.transposition-table.name: Transposition table
term.transposition-table.short: A fixed-size hash table from position to search result, so a position reached by different move orders is searched once.
term.trunk-heads.name: Trunk and heads
term.trunk-heads.short: The shared stack of layers (trunk) that feeds two small output parts (heads), one for policy and one for value.
term.trunk-heads.long: The trunk does the shared work: a first hex convolution and the residual blocks turn the input planes into 32 channels per cell (64 in LARGE). Two heads then read the same trunk output. The policy head computes a 'from' and a 'to' logit per cell; the value head averages over all cells and ends in one tanh output per player.
term.underfitting.name: Underfitting
term.underfitting.short: A model cannot even fit its training data well, usually because it is too small or trained too briefly.
term.underfitting.long: Underfitting is the opposite of overfitting: training and held-out loss are both high. A diagnostic in this project measured it. The targets themselves varied from seed to seed by a median KL of only 0.057, far below the network's held-out KL of about 0.42. So the targets were learnable and the network fell short, which led to the capacity test.
term.value.name: Value
term.value.short: The network's estimate of the final result for each player, from −1 (loss) to +1 (win), without searching further.
term.value.long: The value is the network's second output: one number per player in the range −1 to +1, produced by the tanh at the end of the value head. It plays the role that the evaluation function plays in alpha-beta. MCTS backs it up along the path of each simulation. In self-play training, the value target is the actual game result.
term.vector-api.name: Vector API
term.vector-api.short: The JDK incubator API `jdk.incubator.vector` for SIMD arithmetic in plain Java; `VectorNetwork` uses it for the CPU forward pass.
term.virtual-loss.name: Virtual loss
term.virtual-loss.short: A temporary lost visit on a path in progress, so the descents that fill one batch take different paths.
term.visit-count.name: Visit count
term.visit-count.short: How often the search has passed through a move; MCTS plays the most visited move at the root.
term.warm-up.name: Warm-up
term.warm-up.short: The first steps of a run, in which the learning rate rises linearly from near zero to its base value.
term.warm-up.long: At the start of training the weights are random or come from another stage, and the optimiser's statistics are empty. Full-size steps then can push the weights far off. A warm-up avoids that by raising the learning rate linearly, `lr · (s + 1) / warmup` at step s. Run 1 of generation 0 used 200 warm-up steps.
term.wasm.name: WebAssembly (Wasm)
term.wasm.short: A compact binary code format that browsers run at near-native speed; the default engine is compiled to it.
term.wasm-gc.name: Wasm GC
term.wasm-gc.short: WebAssembly with garbage collection, so Java compiles to it without its own heap manager.
term.web-worker.name: Web Worker
term.web-worker.short: A browser background thread with its own event loop; it shares no objects with the page, only messages.
term.webgpu.name: WebGPU
term.webgpu.short: The browser API for the GPU; the engine `net-webgpu` runs its forward pass with it.
term.weight.name: Weight
term.weight.short: One learned number of a model; in a linear formula, the factor by which one feature is multiplied.
term.weight.long: Weights are the numbers a model learns from data instead of having them set by hand. The linear evaluation has 13 of them, one per feature, found by logistic regression. The SMALL network has about {n:62000}, found by gradient descent. Think of them as the fields of an object that training fills in; the code that uses them never changes.
term.weight-decay.name: Weight decay
term.weight-decay.short: Shrinks the weights slightly at every step to discourage extreme values; here 0.01 on weight tensors.
term.weight-decay.long: Weight decay pulls every weight a little towards zero at each step, so only weights that the data keep pushing stay large. This acts against overfitting; the classic form is called L2 regularisation. The project applies 0.01 to the weight matrices only, not to the biases and not to the two residual-prior scalars. The value was chosen, never varied.
term.weights-bias.name: Weights and bias
term.weights-bias.short: The learned matrix a layer multiplies its input by, and the vector it adds afterwards.
term.weights-bias.long: A layer computes `W · x + b`: the weight matrix W mixes the input values, the bias vector b shifts the result. Both are learned. Together, the weights and biases of all layers are the network's parameters. Weight decay in training shrinks only the weight matrices, not the biases.
term.wgsl.name: WGSL
term.wgsl.short: The shader language of WebGPU; the browser's GPU kernels for the forward pass are written in it.
term.z-score.name: z-score
term.z-score.short: (score − 0.5) / standard error; above 1.28 means better than even with 90 % one-sided confidence.
term.z-score.long: The z-score measures a result in units of its own noise. z = 0 means exactly even; z = 1.96 is the usual two-sided 95 % threshold, which the project uses for paired reports. The gate demands z > 1.28. With that rule, a candidate that is only equally strong passes in 10 % of gates instead of 50 % with 'score above 0.5'.
term.zobrist-hashing.name: Zobrist hashing
term.zobrist-hashing.short: A 64-bit position key: XOR of one random number per (player, cell) and one for the side to move.
term.small-large.name: SMALL and LARGE
term.small-large.short: Two network sizes: SMALL has 32 channels and 4 residual blocks (about {n:62000} weights), LARGE 64 and 6 (about {n:353000}).
term.loop-run.name: Loop run
term.loop-run.short: One training run of the self-play loop with its own settings; the project made seven, numbered 1 to 7.
term.best-spec.name: BEST_SPEC
term.best-spec.short: The strongest classical player: alpha-beta with all options, the evaluator racelin1-r3 and the large race table rows1.bin (about 254 MB).
term.browser-spec.name: BROWSER_SPEC
term.browser-spec.short: The browser's classical player: BEST_SPEC with the race table rows2.bin (about 13 MB); about 56 Elo weaker at equal nodes.
term.jit.name: JIT compiler
term.jit.short: Compiles frequently run bytecode to machine code while the program runs; the reason why benchmarks run a warm-up round first.
term.auto-vectorization.name: Auto-vectorization
term.auto-vectorization.short: The compiler turns an ordinary loop into SIMD instructions by itself; this project does not rely on it.
term.fma.name: FMA (fused multiply-add)
term.fma.short: Computes `a * b + c` in one instruction with one rounding; this project's Vector API code always uses it.
term.vector-species.name: Species (Vector API)
term.vector-species.short: The shape of a vector: its width in bits and its number of lanes, for example 8 floats with AVX2.
term.incubator-module.name: Incubator module
term.incubator-module.short: A JDK API that is not final yet; it needs `--add-modules` and prints a warning at start.
term.value-class.name: Value class (Project Valhalla)
term.value-class.short: A class whose instances have no identity, so a JVM may store them flat; a preview targeted to JDK 28.
term.virtual-thread.name: Virtual thread
term.virtual-thread.short: A thread that the JVM schedules on a few platform threads; a parked virtual thread costs almost nothing.
term.carrier-thread.name: Carrier thread
term.carrier-thread.short: The platform thread on which a virtual thread runs while it is not parked.
term.ffm-api.name: Foreign Function & Memory API
term.ffm-api.short: The JDK API `java.lang.foreign` for memory outside the heap (`MemorySegment`) and for calls into native code.
term.kernel.name: Kernel (GPU)
term.kernel.short: A function that the GPU runs once per work item, thousands of times in parallel.
term.task-graph.name: Task graph (TornadoVM)
term.task-graph.short: TornadoVM's description of the copies and kernels that one execution plan runs.
term.bounds-check.name: Bounds check
term.bounds-check.short: The check that an array index lies inside the array; Java always does it, TornadoVM kernels never do.
term.make-unmake.name: Make/unmake
term.make-unmake.short: Play a move on one mutable position and take it back afterwards, instead of copying the position.
term.cold-start.name: Cold start
term.cold-start.short: The time from the start of a new process to its first result.
term.browser-callable.name: Browser-callable service
term.browser-callable.short: Hilla: a Java class marked `@BrowserCallable`; the build generates a TypeScript client for its public methods.
term.csrf-token.name: CSRF token
term.csrf-token.short: A secret value from a cookie that each call repeats in a header, so other sites cannot call the endpoint.
term.bucket.name: Bucket
term.bucket.short: The batch size rounded up to a power of two; TornadoVM compiles one plan per bucket.
term.kernel-choice-rule.name: Kernel-choice rule
term.kernel-choice-rule.short: Picks the naive convolution kernel while bucket × channels is at most 128, otherwise a tiled kernel.
term.device-thread.name: Device thread
term.device-thread.short: The one thread that collects positions from many games and passes them to the GPU as a batch.
